activities.anchor: the adversary system is the field's peer review
activities.caption: drag the divider — two kinds of scrutiny
activities.name: fsScrutinyCompare

config.prompt: The same result, checked two ways — drag the divider:

before.label: The research lab
before.text: A chemist publishes and invites colleagues to check it over months, at their leisure, mostly sympathetically.

after.label: The courtroom
after.text: A defence expert checks it within weeks, under procedures written into law, paid to break it — and it happens in public.

config.why: Document everything, preserve everything, claim no more than the method supports — every rule exists because of who does the checking.

activities.anchor: asserts that transferred material is nearly always present
activities.caption: pair the principle with its people and places
activities.name: fsLocardMatch

config.prompt: Locard's principle and its origins — pair each piece:

pairs.right: the first police laboratory opens — two attic rooms
Edmond Locard, who proved the principle case by case

config.why: The crowbar picks up paint from the window frame; the frame keeps metal smears from the crowbar — two-way transfer, both useful, and glass fragments survive in a cuff lining for weeks.

activities.anchor: whose product is not conclusions but
activities.caption: line up the scene examiner's sequence
activities.name: fsSceneOrder

config.prompt: The first room, in working order — sequence the scene examiner's moves:
items: document everything in situ — photographs, sketching, notes
search systematically — grids, spirals, zones, so coverage is provable
collect and package each item separately
record the chain of custody — every transfer signed and dated
config.why: The chain is what turns a physical object into evidence: an unbroken record survives cross-examination, and a gap is a gift to the defence — a broken chain has sunk otherwise airtight cases.

activities.caption: file each job under its bench
activities.name: fsBenchSort

config.prompt: Inside the second room — file each task under its discipline:

items.label: short-tandem-repeat profiles, sensitive enough to reach a few cells
fibres, glass, paint, gunshot residue, soil
comparing striations and impressions under the microscope
AFIS proposing candidates for a human examiner to compare

config.why: Document and digital examination — handwriting, ink, and now terabytes of devices — round out the modern lab.

activities.anchor: is doing its job, not failing it
activities.caption: run the lab — two quality tests
activities.name: fsLabBranch

config.root: You run an accredited laboratory. A busy police force wants one word; your result says another.

start.text: The force wants 'matching'. Your analysis says 'inconclusive'. What goes in the report?

choices.label: Report it as the evidence says
choices.feedback: Independence from the outcome is a defining feature — under accreditation to standards like ISO 17025, the answer belongs to the evidence.

choices.label: Soften the wording to keep the investigation happy
choices.feedback: That is the failure mode: the client of a forensic result is the court, not the investigation's outcome.

end.text: Two features define the system's quality: accreditation to standards, and independence from the outcome.

config.why: An unchallengeable analysis with a one-day gap in the custody log is worthless; a modest result with an impeccable record is usable.

activities.anchor: The distinction is epistemological, not cosmetic
activities.caption: find the faulty line — two tiers of claim
activities.name: fsTierSpot

config.prompt: One line of this evidence-grammar note is wrong — click it:
lines: Class characteristics place evidence in a group: a blue acrylic fibre, a size 10 training shoe, a 2010s red Honda.
Individual characteristics can tie evidence to a single source: random wear marks on a barrel, a full DNA profile, unique ridge detail.
The two tiers are just labels — a formality of bookkeeping with no consequence.
Class narrows a population to a group; individual points to a source.
Methods drifting between the tiers is a recurring story in the discipline's history.
config.correction: The boundary between 'consistent with' and 'came from' decides which claims each tier of evidence licenses.
config.why: A full short-tandem-repeat profile reaches the source tier because the chance of two unrelated people sharing it is billions to one, calculated from measured allele frequencies — several pattern disciplines drifted into source-level language without equivalent statistics.

activities.anchor: DNA earned its place in the individual tier
activities.caption: call the rarity before the reveal
activities.name: fsRarityEstimate

config.prompt: Two strangers walk into a lab. The chance they share a full short-tandem-repeat profile is roughly one in —?
config.why: Billions to one — astronomically small, calculated from measured allele frequencies; that statistics is what lets a profile point to a single person.

activities.caption: bet on the honest verdict line
activities.name: fsCsiPredict

config.q: Real casework often cannot split the final candidates. What is the most scientifically valuable statement an examiner can give the court?
choices: A definitive match, announced the same day
'Consistent with X, inconsistent with Y, cannot distinguish between Z and W'
'The evidence proves the suspect did it'
config.why: Analyses take weeks, results are probabilistic, evidence is often degraded, mixed or absent — fighting the 'CSI effect' with honest likelihood language is part of the job.
